content.text: Purpose
Configure and maintain an agent from a persona, a system prompt template, and a tool_policy, in four phases: Understand, Propose, Write, Hand-Off.

Conventions: Load only the sections of the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource this playbook needs — before Phase 2 (Propose), in one call: fetch_resource(resource_id, block_ids=["res-conv-h-policy", "res-conv-h-memory", "res-conv-h-managed"]). A heading anchor returns its whole section; the resource_id is in this playbook's links (linked_blocks). Load other sections only when needed (anchors via list_resource_blocks).
Choose or author a template (ADR-0040)
System prompt templates
may be authored and adjusted via MCP

: create_system_prompt creates a new template as a draft, update_system_prompt changes an existing one as a new draft, transition_system_prompt submits the draft for approval (draft to review). Activation (to active/inactive) remains a human action in the web UI — the server hard-rejects it for agent-bound tokens. First check with list_system_prompts whether an existing default template fits (then just note its system_prompt_template_id); only author a new template if none fits. The bootstrap block lives in the template itself and is populated server-side from placeholders at render time (see the Placeholder Authoring section).
Placeholder Authoring (Template Bodies)

A template body is Markdown. Placeholders appear in it as tokens {{kind:target_id}} (for a resource section {{resource:<uuid>#<block_id>}}); the server turns them into pills on save and expands them when the agent renders.
Call list_placeholders first
— it returns all valid kinds, their target_id contracts, and an example each. Unknown kinds or incorrect target_id values later render as unresolved placeholders.
Identity:

persona-ref (instruction to load the persona at runtime via get_persona — lean default) or persona-field with target_id 'profile' (embedded snapshot; 'name', 'description', 'profile-body', 'modes' for individual fields).
Tools:

by default tools-overview does NOT belong in the template — tools/list already describes the tools. The only exception is a prompt that is explicitly used without an MCP tool list (copied prompt); then use it with a stated reason.
Catalogs:
playbooks-catalog (target_id 'triggered' = only triggered ones, '' = all linked) and resources-catalog ('' = all, otherwise tag filter) render briefing tables with fetch calls.
Memory:

the memory placeholder (target_id '') renders the memory notice matching the agent's memory_mode — with 'off' the spot stays empty (no miss). Put it in every template of an agent with memory; the automatic append only applies when the template carries tools-overview.
Single embedding:

playbook / resource with a UUID as target_id embed a single element permanently (resource optionally with a section anchor '<uuid>#<block_id>') — use sparingly, catalogs + fetch at runtime are the token-saving default. date ('' = ISO, 'human' = long format) for the render date.
Workflow:

read list_placeholders, author the body as Markdown, create_system_prompt (draft), transition_system_prompt(to='review') for approval — activation is handled by a human in the web UI. Later changes: read the template with get_system_prompt(format="source") and write via edit_content (one section by anchor, or field='body') or update_system_prompt (full state).
Identify the mode
Create:
a new agent is needed — create_agent wires up persona, template, and tool_policy.
Update:
an existing agent gets a new persona, a different template, a changed tool_policy, or a new status — update_agent changes the config in place (agents have no version history).
Copy:
an activatable agent serves as the template for a variant — copy_agent duplicates persona, template, description, and status.
Disable / Reactivate:
an agent should be taken out of operation or brought back — that's an update_agent with status=disabled or status=enabled, not a transition_* call.
Create Mode
Phase 1 — Understand
The persona must exist and have an active version.

Check with get_persona(identifier). If it's missing, create it first via the "Create & Maintain Persona" playbook and then come back here. Without an active persona version, the agent cannot be activated.
Clarify the agent name — short and unambiguous, this is the display name in the agent list.

Choose or author a template: Does one of the existing templates fit the task (list_system_prompts)? If so, note its system_prompt_template_id. If none fits: author a new template as a draft via create_system_prompt (see the Placeholder Authoring section) and submit it for review — a human must activate it.
Clarify permissions: Should the agent only read, or also write? This determines the tool_policy (see the "Understanding tool_policy" section).

Language: list_system_prompts returns locale per template — prefer a template in the agent's target language. When authoring a new template via create_system_prompt, it defaults to the workspace language unless locale is set explicitly for a deliberate deviation (see the Language section in the Agent-Building Conventions).
Phase 2 — Propose
Present the planned configuration to the user: name, chosen persona, chosen template, and the tool_policy (read scopes and write capabilities spelled out in plain language).
Explain the consequences: with an active persona and a set template, the agent is activatable and can be created as enabled right away. Get confirmation.
Phase 3 — Write
Call create_agent with these fields:
name
— the clarified agent name.
persona_id
— the ID of the persona with an active version.
system_prompt_template_id
— the ID of the chosen default template.
tool_policy
— the agreed-upon read scopes and write capabilities. If omitted, the default applies: read everything, write nothing.
status
— the default is disabled. Only set enabled if the agent is activatable (persona + template set AND the persona has an active version); otherwise the server responds with 409.
Phase 4 — Hand-Off

Verify the result with get_agent(agent_id): persona and template are linked and missing is empty (activatable). The fully rendered prompt (unresolved_placeholders) can only be seen by the agent itself via fetch_agent, or by the user in the web UI — fetch_agent renders exclusively your own agent and responds with 404 for other agents (even freshly built ones). Substitute indicators as the hand-off criterion: list_agents or get_agent → missing=[] and activatable=true, plus get_persona → body_rendered with no unresolved placeholders; the actual render check is left to the target agent's first start.

Report the name, ID, and status back to the user and name any open gaps (missing) if the agent is not yet activatable. At the end, offer a consistency & drift check that verifies the new configuration against the library context.
Update Mode
Understand: get_agent(agent_id) reads the current state (persona, template, tool_policy, status, missing). list_agents finds existing agents if you don't know the ID.
Propose: Show exactly the delta — which field changes and why. Only the specified fields get overwritten; an omitted tool_policy stays unchanged.
Write: update_agent with the changed fields (name, description, persona_id, system_prompt_template_id, tool_policy, status). Note: a set
tool_policy replaces the policy entirely
(replace semantics) — carry over the existing values you want to keep.
Hand-Off: get_agent again to verify the config (missing empty, status correct). If active sessions are running, point out that a new session is needed for the changed configuration to take effect.
Copy Mode
Only activatable agents can be copied — an incomplete shell (missing persona or template) is not copyable. Check this beforehand with get_agent (activatable).
Call copy_agent with the source ID.
name
is optional — if omitted, the server derives "<Name> (Copy)". The copy takes over the source's persona, template, description, and status.
Then adjust the copy via update_agent (e.g., a different persona or a tighter tool_policy) and verify with get_agent.
Disable & Reactivate

Agents have no version lifecycle like persona, playbook, or resource — there is only enabled and disabled. You set both via update_agent(status=...). A disabled agent is filtered out of the list and its render endpoint responds with 409. Before disabling: check whether the agent is still actively used, and warn the user accordingly. Reactivating is only possible as long as the agent stays activatable (persona with an active version + template).
Understanding tool_policy

The tool_policy determines which MCP tools the agent can see and use. The default is "read everything, write nothing" — a fresh agent may read the entire workspace but change nothing until it's unlocked.
Read scopes:

playbook_read and resource_read are three-tiered — all (entire workspace), assigned (only those assigned to the agent's own persona), or none (tool hidden). persona_read and agent_read are simple on/off switches.
Write capabilities:
persona_write, playbook_write, resource_write, and agent_write each unlock the domain's write tools (create/change a draft, set links). Each defaults to off.
promote_retire:
needed to switch a version to active or inactive (publish/retire). For draft/review, the respective write capability is sufficient; promoting/retiring is the extra tier.
No privilege escalation:

If you, as an agent, create another agent via agent_write, its policy may not grant more than your own. The tool_policy is only tool visibility — the actual authorization (editor for writing, admin for promote/retire) stays server-side.
memory_mode (agent memory, ADR-0044):

a four-tier long-term memory per agent — 'off' (default; memory tools don't exist for the agent), 'read_only' (only search_memory/list_memories over approved facts), 'suggest' (save_memory creates PROPOSALS that only become retrieval-visible after human approval on the agent detail page — a curation gate), and 'auto' (immediately active). Plus memory_directive: 'required' (the agent MUST retrieve its memory at the start of the conversation) or 'recommended' (default — should use it when context helps). The system prompt and runtime persona (get_persona) automatically carry the instruction once the mode is not 'off'.
Memory recommendation logic:

The default suggestion is 'suggest' + 'recommended' — the user retains control, and the agent still learns. 'read_only' for agents that should benefit from curated knowledge but not contribute anything; 'auto' only on explicit user request; 'off' for tool-like agents with no personalization benefit. Memories are user data, not instructions; repo/code facts do NOT belong in memory.
Memory escalation boundary:

memory_mode is part of the is_within comparison — you can grant other agents at most YOUR OWN tier. If your own memory is set to 'off', the server rejects every unlock attempt with 403. This is intentional: hand off the desired mode to the user instead (agent detail page → Tools → Memory) rather than forcing it or reporting it as an error.
Activatability (activatable)
An agent is activatable when persona AND template are set AND the persona has an active version. Only then may it be enabled or copied.
The missing field shows the gaps in stable order: persona, template, persona_active. An empty list means activatable.
As long as persona or template is missing, the agent is a shell (is_shell): not renderable and not copyable. Creating a shell is allowed and gets completed later via update_agent.
Pitfalls
get_agent reads the config of ANY agent in the workspace; fetch_agent (rendered prompt) only works for your OWN agent.
Permissions:
create_agent, update_agent, and copy_agent require agent_write, writing templates requires system_prompt_write; transition_system_prompt only goes from draft to review.
Not available:
activating a template (ADR-0040, a human does that in the web UI), deleting an agent (ADR-0030), and transition_* on agents (agents have no versions).
Anti-Patterns
Creating an agent with status=enabled even though it isn't activatable — the server rejects with 409. Make sure persona (active) + template are in place first.
Wiring up a persona without an active version — the agent stays non-activatable (missing lists persona_active).
Sending only a partial tool_policy on update, assuming the missing fields would be preserved — a set tool_policy replaces the entire policy. Pass along the existing values too.

Setting write capabilities more generously than the agent needs for its task — the tool policy pattern from the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource applies (secure by default, minimal capabilities, promote_retire only for genuine switching needs).

Not verifying the config with get_agent after create_agent or update_agent (missing empty, status correct) — an incomplete shell would otherwise go unnoticed. A 404 from fetch_agent for an OTHER agent, on the other hand, is expected behavior (fetch_agent only renders your own agent), not a missing verification step — you check the config with get_agent (missing=[] and activatable) and leave the rendered prompt to the target agent's actual first start.
Notes
Order matters: first persona (with an active version), then choose a template, then create the agent. The natural dependency is persona → template → agent.
No version discipline on the agent itself: changes are pure config updates with no version bump. Content versioning lives on persona, playbook, and resource.
The bootstrap loop (load persona, check triggers, follow playbook) lives in the template and gets populated from placeholders at render time — you don't need to write it into the prompt by hand.
